grid.layout: layout x,y; cell (gx,gy) = (round(x/1000*(G-1)), round(y/1000*(G-1))); row-major, row = gy (y downward), index = gy*G+gx
grid.encoding: u8 base64: U = -5 + byte/255*(3--5); U = -log(q + 0.05); q = smoothed arrival density / its sum * G^2 (q=1 uniform)

method: Each model's smoothed arrival density p_m (all arrivals, the same grid, sigma 2.6 cells and weighting as the per-model terrain table) is shrunk toward the pooled-agents density p_pool: p_shrunk = (n_m p_m + k p_pool) / (n_m + k), n_m = number of runs of the model, then U = -log(q + 0.05) and the same uint8 quantisation. k = 200 pseudo-runs, chosen by split-half cross-validation: for each model 40 random half-splits of its runs; the density from one half (n = half the runs), shrunk toward a pool that excludes the held-out half, is scored on the other half by mean log-likelihood of that half's arrivals (1% uniform floor); k maximising the mean over the 8 models (equal weight) is used. Held-out correlation of U cannot choose k: it keeps rising with k up to the grid maximum (3000) because a pure pool correlates best with any noisy half, so it rewards ignoring the model; it is reported in k_selection only. split_half_raw = correlation of U between two raw halves; split_half_shrunk = correlation of U(shrunk half) with U(raw other half), averaged over both directions (not shrunk-vs-shrunk, which a shared pool would inflate); both at half n, so pessimistic for the full-n terrain. sparse = weight < 0.5 or split_half_raw < 0.3.

readers.coverage_note: step-1 neighbourhoods of the 20 start pages only
readers.mask_encoding: np.packbits of a G*G boolean (row-major, same cell index as data), bit 1 = covered (cell within 40 layout units of a reader target page); outside the mask readers have no information

caption: Terrains of single models rest on few runs, so each is blended with the all-agents terrain in proportion to how little data the model has; where a model looks like the pooled terrain, that is the blend, not a finding.
